note: A Web Push body (RFC 8291) written by src/main/push/webpush.ts. The Android suite decrypts it with the keys below; both sides also check that each can read what the other wrote.
$register: The WEBPUSH lines, exactly as they go on the wire. The keys are one parameter with a semicolon in it, not two parameters — the desktop sent two, so a server read the public key as the whole of it, never saw the auth secret, and refused every registration the feature ever attempted. rIRCd's HELP WEBPUSH states the shape and tests/smoke/test_webpush.py in that repo sends it.
$refusals: What rIRCd answers, so a client knows which of these is worth retrying and which is the user's to fix. None of them are retryable by sending the same line again.

refusals.name: not logged in
refusals.meaning: A push endpoint outlives the connection that made it, so it belongs to an account rather than to whoever holds a nick.

refusals.name: keys missing or malformed
refusals.meaning: Both p256dh and auth, in one parameter, separated by a semicolon.
